name: Question 2
problem: The curve $C$ is the intersection of a surface $S,$ defined by $z=f(x,y),$ with the plane $y=2.$ Given that the point $P(1,2,1)$ lies on $C$, and that ${f}_{x}=2xy+2$, find the equations of the tangent line to $C$ at $P.$
worked_solution:
The curve $C$ is the intersection of the surface $z=f(x,y)$ with the plane $y=2.$ Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point $P(1,2,1)$ will be given by the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,2)}.$

To get the slope, we evaluate the partial derivative $\frac{∂z}{∂x}$ at $(1,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,2)} & =2(1)(2)+2 \\  & =4+2 \\  & =6\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

$$
\begin{aligned}z-z{|}_{(1,2)} & =\frac{∂z}{∂x}{|}_{(1,2)}(x-1) \\ z-1 & =6(x-1) \\ z & =6x-5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the tangent line to the curve $C$ at $P(1,2,1)$ can be given as the intersection of two planes, as follows:

$$
{\begin{aligned}y=2 \\ z=6x-5\end{aligned}
$$

The curve C is the intersection of a surface S, defined by z=f(x,y), with the plane y=2. Given that the point P(1,2,1) lies on C, and that fx=2xy+2, find the equations of the tangent line to C at P.

a
{y=2z=6x+3
b
{y=2z=3x−2
c
{y=2z=3x−5
d
{y=2z=4x+3
e
{y=2z=6x−5

EXPLANATION

The curve C is the intersection of the surface z=f(x,y) with the plane y=2. Hence, the slope of the tangent to the curve at the point P(1,2,1) will be given by the partial derivative ∂z∂x|(1,2).

∂z∂x|(1,2)=2(1)(2)+2=4+2=6

Now, we use the point-slope form of a straight line:

z−z|(1,2)=∂z∂x|(1,2)(x−1)z−1=6(x−1)z=6x−5
